samples.summary: User/peer-controlled `color` and `backgroundColor` strings are interpolated unescaped into DOCX XML attributes, while the sibling `fontFamily` on the same element is explicitly escaped for exactly this reason
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:73` emits `<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>` and :77 `<w:shd ... w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"/>`; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:311` does the same for table-cell background. Only `#` is stripped — no `escapeXmlAttr`, even though the same file defines one at :25 with a comment stating font/style values "originate from untrusted sources (PPTX/DOCX imports, user input in the font picker)". Attack path: (a) victim imports a hostile .docx — `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62` stores `style.color = '#' + val` with `val` taken verbatim from the attacker's `<w:color w:val=...>`, no format validation; or (b) a collaborator on a shared doc writes an arbitrary `color`/`backgroundColor` Yorkie tree attribute, which `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:177-178` (`parseInlineStyle`) accepts as any string. When the victim then exports to DOCX, a value like `000"/><w:rStyle w:val="x` (or containing `<`/`&`) escapes the attribute and injects arbitrary OOXML into the file the victim downloads/redistributes, at minimum corrupting it and at worst smuggling attacker-chosen run/document markup. This code is pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff is the color write boundary and its own comment claims to fix what "export paths" see, so the color→export chain is squarely the change's subject matter.

samples.summary: The new `normalizeStyleClears` write boundary special-cases `''` but performs no validation of color values; nothing anywhere in the docs inline-style write path constrains `color`/`backgroundColor` to a hex/StoredColor shape
samples.evidence: `normalizeStyleClears` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:277-286) is described in the accompanying task doc as "the single point where a stored run is produced", yet it only maps `''`→`undefined` and passes every other string through. I grepped the write path (`applyInlineStyle` in packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:313, `applyStyle`/`applyStyles`/`applyStyleInTree` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1698/1734/1784, `serializeInlineStyle`:107, `parseInlineStyle`:166, `defaultColorResolver` in packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:14) and found no hex/format check on any of them. Consequence: arbitrary attacker-chosen strings (from DOCX import, from a collaborating peer's CRDT attribute, from clipboard style parsing) are persisted as colors and handed to downstream consumers that interpolate them into markup (see the DOCX finding). Adding a cheap `/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/`-style guard at this boundary — or at `parseInlineStyle` — would close the class rather than one sink. Impact rated minor on its own because it is hardening; the concrete sink is reported separately.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed and is unguarded. docx-style-map.ts:73 emits `<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>` and :77 emits `<w:shd ... w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"/>` with no XML attribute escaping, while the same file defines escapeXmlAttr at :25-32 (comment: style values "originate from untrusted sources (PPTX/DOCX imports, user input in the font picker)") and applies it to fontFamily at :53-56. defaultColorResolver (model/color.ts:14-22) returns any string verbatim — no hex validation exists anywhere in the docs package (the only `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` check is in an unrelated slides theme-builder UI). Untrusted ingress is real and unvalidated: import/docx-style-map.ts:62 sets style.color = '#'+val directly from the attacker-supplied `<w:color w:val>` attribute (and :76 from shd/@fill), and frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:177-178 accepts peer-supplied color/backgroundColor as arbitrary strings. docx-exporter.ts:309-311 repeats the unescaped interpolation for table-cell shading. Since the DOM parser decodes entities, a hostile .docx can smuggle raw `"`, `<`, `&` into the stored color, which is re-emitted unescaped on export, breaking out of the attribute and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into the file the victim downloads/redistributes. This is unsafe input handling / injection — in-lane for the security rubric — and no guard, validator, or caller-side sanitizer makes it unreachable.
